name: Game on Axis
description: There are $$$n$$$ points $$$1,2,\ldots,n$$$, each point $$$i$$$ has a number $$$a_i$$$ on it. You're playing a game on them. Initially, you are at point $$$1$$$. When you are at point $$$i$$$, take following steps: If $$$1\le i\le n$$$, go to $$$i+a_i$$$, Otherwise, the game ends. Before the game begins, you can choose two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ satisfying $$$1\le x\le n$$$, $$$-n \le y \le n$$$ and replace $$$a_x$$$ with $$$y$$$ (set $$$a_x := y$$$). Find the number of distinct pairs $$$(x,y)$$$ such that the game that you start after making the change ends in a finite number of steps. Notice that you do not have to satisfy $$$a_x\not=y$$$.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 10^4)$$$ — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of points. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ ($$$-n \le a_i \le n$$$) — the numbers on the axis. It's guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ does not exceed $$$2\cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print a line containing a single integer — the number of distinct pairs $$$(x,y)$$$ with which the game ends.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1787D — Game on Axis [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
